$comment: Allow-list record for the repo ROOT and docs/. scripts/check-manifest.mjs can validate it explicitly, but it is not a `pnpm gate` or CI rung. Adding a NEW top-level root entry, or a NEW standalone doc under docs/, REQUIRES adding it here with a justification first — that friction is the point: it blocks temp/ad-hoc junk at root and keeps durable project knowledge in the Library (definition/principle/pattern/guardrail/techstack/adr/open-question), not loose prose docs. A new doc's justification must say why it does NOT belong in the Library. See the `repo-surface-allowlist` Library guardrail.

packageOwnership.$comment: The organism-boundary ownership map (ADR-0074, amended by ADR-0075), read by packages/cli/src/check-boundaries.ts (`pnpm check:boundaries`, wired into `pnpm gate` + the CI verify job). Every @storytree/* package under packages/* is classified EXACTLY once as an `organism` (owned by one story). The gate asserts every real runtime cross-organism dependency edge (each package.json `dependencies`; devDeps are test scaffolding and excluded, ADR-0010 §5) is COVERED by a declared cross-story edge — consumer-side in the consumer story's `depends_on`, OR provider-side in the provider story's `consumed_by` (stories/*/story.md, ADR-0074 §4) — so cross-organism coupling can't be added without a declared edge, and because the studio forest renders `depends_on`, every coupling is therefore UI-visible. NOTE (ADR-0075, 2026-06-19; the ports renamed for role-not-position per ADR-0078, 2026-06-20): the shared ports storage-protocol/proof-protocol are NO LONGER an exempt `substrate` class — they are ordinary ROOT organisms (stories/storage-protocol + stories/proof-protocol, depends_on [] / [proof-protocol]) that every consumer DECLARES depends_on, exactly like cli/store stopped being exempt 'composition roots' in ADR-0074 §2. They stay listed in `foundational` (a SUBSET of organisms, not a class) to carry ONE minimality rule the gate enforces — a foundational port may only depend on another foundational port — which keeps them zod-only / node+pg-free so the studio's browser bundle works. So a port dependency is a visible declared+rendered edge, not an invisible exemption.
packageOwnership.$comment_surfaces: Consuming SURFACES (ADR-0100): a surface name → the story that owns it. A surface is an apps/* app (the studio) — a sink that wires organisms together and is consumed by nothing. ADR-0100 brought apps/* into the same boundary scan as packages/*: a surface's package.json @storytree/* deps are COVERED by the same rule as an organism's (declared in the surface's own story depends_on), so the studio's real wiring is enforced + rendered, exactly the visibility-over-exemption call ADR-0074 §2 made for the cli/store hubs. A surface is never `foundational` and draws no inbound edge. (The public-website subrepo is also a consuming surface but ships no workspace package — its forest-world edge is a declared story node backed by the check:web-engine drift gate, ADR-0093, not a package scanned here.)

sourceOwnership.$comment: The SECOND declared ownership map (ADR-0317 D2), at SUBTREE grain — the `packageOwnership` pattern one level down, read by packages/cli/src/ownership.ts (`storytree ownership`). `packageOwnership` above answers 'which story owns this PACKAGE' and check:boundaries holds it to the disk at 24/24. Nothing answered 'which addressable unit is responsible for this FILE', and the natural candidate cannot: `proof.real.sourceFile` is typed `sourceFile: string`, a total function unit→the one file that unit AUTHORS, so it inverts into ownership neither surjectively (its image is bounded by the 296-node count, not the 519 files) nor injectively (apps/studio/src/components/TreeView.tsx is named by SEVEN units). That field is NOT decayed — 111 owned against 117 declared-and-existing targets, ~95% full — it simply was never an ownership map, and `scope.sourceGlobs` is a per-phase WRITE FENCE deliberately broader than what a unit owns (which is why check-boundaries.ts:227 filters globs out of the proof-bound set). NEITHER field is read here and neither changes: the prove-it-gate, the phase machine, the write scopes and every signed verdict carry ZERO risk from this map. GLOBS ARE PERMITTED HERE and refused there, because this map binds no verdict. VALUE = an addressable object in the work graph: a CAPABILITY id by preference (the grain claims are taken at, ADR-0270 D1), or a story id where no capability is the honest answer; ADR-0317 D3 makes a declared subtree itself claimable. REPORT-ONLY: `storytree ownership` renders this and fails nothing, and a BLOCKING rung must earn its place on this report's own numbers first (ADR-0311 retired sixteen rungs for want of evidence). ### AUTHORED IN FULL 2026-08-06 (first-class-edges-arc), 527 of 527 files owned, and three authoring rules the next editor must keep. (1) MIXED GRAIN, WITH THE SPLIT REPORTED. Capability grain wherever a capability's stated outcome names or plainly covers the subtree's job; story grain only where the tree HAS no such capability. Measured on landing: 363 files (68.9%) capability-grain, 164 (31.1%) story-grain. Story grain is legal (ADR-0317 D3) but it satisfies totality while leaving 'claim the capability you are writing' nothing finer to bind to — which is the arc's founding measurement, now COUNTED instead of assumed. The residual IS the story-author worklist — but only the `residue` CLASS of it, and the grain count is not that class: measured 2026-08-14, 20 of the 92 story-grain declarations are DECIDED by rules (1) and (4) below (17 barrels + 3 stories declaring no units), so driving the grain number itself to zero would mean un-deciding them. `storytree ownership` now splits the three and gives each its own remedy. It is OWNED, and it MOVES BOTH WAYS — ask `storytree ownership` for the live grain line rather than quoting a figure from here, because it drains as capabilities are authored and ACCRUES as new code lands story-grain. Re-measured 2026-08-07 BEFORE increment 2 landed against it: 372 of 537 files (69.3%) capability-grain, 165 (30.7%) story-grain, concentrated in `cli` 51 (gate rungs, drains, generated-view builders, doctors), `studio` 39, `desktop` 12 (increment 2 took that owner to 5 — see rule (5)), `app-surface` 8, `drive-machinery` 8. The owner is `capability-layer-coverage-arc` (chartered 2026-08-07): every story-grain declaration is resolved either into a capability that STATES ITS PROOF or into a recorded one-competence decision — and a count driven to zero by authoring unprovable capabilities is that arc's stated FAILURE mode, not its goal, so do NOT read a falling number here as progress on its own. Two of the story-grain owners are NOT gaps — `proof-protocol` (8) and `storage-protocol` (6) are root-port stories that carry no capabilities because the story IS the one competence. NO BLANKET BUCKET: every owner here names a real object in the work graph (`storytree ownership` resolves all 372 and reports 0 unresolved); an invented 'substrate' owner would drive the number down while changing nothing. (2) DECLARATIONS ARE DISJOINT — never a specific entry plus a broader one covering it. The judge collects EVERY match and reports a second one as CONTESTED regardless of key order, so the ordering-based 'specific before broad' pattern would light that warning permanently over 350+ files — every file sitting under a specific entry — and destroy the signal. Order is therefore free here and contested==0 means what it says. Use `<dir>/*.ts` for a non-recursive directory (`*` never crosses `/`) when a subdirectory needs a different owner; a bare `<dir>` claims everything beneath it and is right only where the whole tree is one competence (packages/forest-world/src, packages/procedural-architecture/src/buildings). (3) THE ENTRY COUNT IS 372, NOT 'tens'. ADR-0317 expected subtree grain to keep entries in the tens; measured, the economy holds where directories are homogeneous (24 packageOwnership entries; forest-world in one line) and breaks in FLAT, HETEROGENEOUS src/ directories where ownership genuinely varies file by file — packages/cli/src is 100 files fronting ~20 different organisms. 372:527 is what totality actually costs here. A new file lands UNOWNED and must be declared; that is the totality check working, and it is why no catch-all is left to swallow it silently. ### (4) A PACKAGE BARREL IS STORY GRAIN BY NATURE, NOT A GAP — added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 1, generalising rule (1)'s `proof-protocol`/`storage-protocol` note from whole stories down to individual subtrees. A `src/index.ts` that only re-exports its package's public surface is the STORY's front door: it is the union of every organ the package fronts, so no single capability is responsible for it and a capability that claimed it would be claiming its siblings' code. Declaring it at story grain is therefore the DECIDED answer, not a residue awaiting a capability — the same reasoning that makes a root-port story one competence, applied one level down. Recorded here rather than per-entry because the map is key→owner with no room for a note. Settled this way in increment 1: `packages/drive/src/index.ts`, `packages/orchestrator/src/index.ts`, `packages/orchestrator/src/store/index.ts`. The rule generalises — counted 2026-08-07, SIXTEEN story-grain declarations are bare `src/index.ts` barrels — a figure that is now DERIVED rather than hand-kept (2026-08-14, ownership-map-holds-totality): `storytree ownership` classifies EVERY story-grain declaration as `barrel` / `no-capability-declared` / `residue` and prints each with its subtree key, so ask it rather than quoting this number, which has already moved to 17; the three named above are settled here and the remaining THIRTEEN sit across the long tail (`agent`, `library`, `app-surface`, `notice-board`, `model-uat*`, `uat-criterion`, `context-traversal-*`, `website-experience`), so that tail is decidable BY THIS RULE and does not need per-file judgment. THE RULE IS ABOUT RE-EXPORT BARRELS ONLY: an `index.ts` carrying real logic is ordinary code and gets the rule (1) treatment. READ IT AS THE DEFAULT ANSWER FOR A BARREL, NOT AS A CLAIM ABOUT WHAT THIS MAP ALREADY SAYS — one live declaration does not match it and is deliberately left alone: `packages/cli/src/index.ts` is a pure re-export barrel (26 lines, every line a re-export) yet is declared to the CAPABILITY `unified-command-dispatch`, alongside `main.ts`/`commands.ts`/`envelope.ts`. Whether to re-point it belongs to `capability-layer-coverage-arc`, not to this rule: re-pointing a declaration ahead of authoring the organ is the opening move that arc explicitly forbids. One more subtree was settled at story grain in increment 1 on the separate ground that it is not an ORGAN: `packages/drive/src/doctrine.ts`, 39 lines rendering one fail-soft CLI doctrine-pointer line, with no colocated test (it is exercised through the `packages/cli` shim). Authoring a capability over it would have breached the arc's hard constraint that a capability must state its own proof. ### (5) FOR A LODGER, COUNT THE CALL SITES BEFORE RE-HOMING IT — added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 2. A LODGER is code sitting in a package it reaches many consumers from rather than one the owning story is responsible for (increment 1 named the pattern in `packages/drive`; it is the dominant difficulty in the residue, and in `cli` and `studio` the question is usually 'WHICH STORY owns this?' rather than 'which capability?'). The tempting move is to re-home it to whichever story its file header or its originating survey names. That move is wrong often enough to need a check, and the check OPENS mechanically: ENUMERATE THE CALL SITES AND SEE WHAT FRACTION BELONG TO THE CANDIDATE STORY. Demonstrated on `apps/desktop/src/backend/open-link-policy.ts`, which this arc proposed re-homing to `embedded-terminal` on the strength of its header (it came from the embedded-terminal patterns survey) and a live precedent (`pty-session-manager` already owns a sibling file in that same directory). `story-author` refused: only ONE of its three call sites is terminal-scoped (`terminal:open-link`), while the other two — `will-navigate` and `setWindowOpenHandler` — are the whole-window navigation lockdown protecting every preload bridge (ADR-0109 §Decision 4). Re-homing would have filed the desktop shell's navigation lockdown under a story that draws no edge to the shell. A header names a module's ORIGIN; the call sites name its JOB, and ownership follows the job. Note the two findings are independent: the call-site count decides WHICH STORY, and the organ test then decides whether a capability exists there at all — this file failed the second too (37 lines, one pure predicate, three isolated unit tests, no integration proof available) and stayed at story grain under rule (1). TWO FENCES ON THIS RULE, both supplied by its own demonstration. THE FRACTION POINTS; THE READING DECIDES. 1-of-3 did not settle `open-link-policy.ts` by arithmetic — it settled it because the two non-terminal sites are a qualitatively DIFFERENT JOB, and their own comments say so: `main.ts:502` (`will-navigate`) and `:508` (`setWindowOpenHandler`) exist because the top frame 'must never be steered off the app's own origin' or an attacker link 'would otherwise inherit the shell-spawn bridge'. Re-verified on the bytes at HEAD 2026-08-07 by the pre-merge librarian pass rather than taken from this note: the enumeration is exactly three call sites and the split is exactly 1/2. A 2-of-3 split across call sites doing the SAME job would decide nothing, so never report the ratio without the reading that goes with it. AND THIS IS A JUDGMENT AID FOR WHAT TO DECLARE, NEVER A DERIVATION OF THE MAP. ADR-0317 D2 REJECTS deriving ownership from the import graph — it would encode who DEPENDS ON a file rather than who is RESPONSIBLE for it, would attribute shared substrate to all 45 stories, and its errors would be silent and indistinguishable from its correct answers — and that rejection stands here unweakened. What this rule licenses is reading the call sites of ONE lodger already under question, to inform a DECLARED answer; nothing is computed over the repo, and a session that reads it as 'derive the map from imports' has inverted the decision this map sits under. ### (6) A GATE INSTRUMENT HOMES TO THE STORY WHOSE TEST SURFACE GOES RED WHEN THE THING DRIFTS — added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 3, and recorded because it CORRECTS a plausible generalisation that increment itself proposed and `story-author` refuted. `packages/cli/src` hosts many check-gate instruments, and increment 3 opened by arguing from an apparent pattern: a gate instrument is homed to the story that owns the CHECKED THING rather than to `cli` — citing `check-process-graph.ts` -> `library-health-gate` (story `library`), `check-web-grounding.ts` -> `website`, `check-declared.ts` -> `claim-at-declare`, and `*boundaries*.ts` -> `organism-boundary-tooling`. THE PATTERN IS NOT UNIFORM, AND THE LAST CITATION BREAKS IT: `organism-boundary-tooling` is a capability of story `cli`, and it is the closest structural twin in the corpus to the case under question — a pure judge plus a check gatherer in `packages/cli/src`, sitting at the immediately adjacent step in `gate-order.ts`. Read as a rule about WHOSE SUBJECT MATTER the gate inspects, the precedent set is mixed and decides nothing. What actually carries is that precedent's OWN stated criterion: `organism-boundary-tooling` is homed to `cli` because it rides the CLI's test surface — `boundaries.test.ts` goes red when it breaks. So the operative question is not whose subject matter is inspected but WHOSE SUITE OBSERVES THE DRIFT: home the instrument where a drift makes a test go red, because binding an outcome to a suite that cannot fail on it is the rubber stamp ADR-0097 §2 forbids (§2 is captioned as RE-AFFIRMING ADR-0085, which is where the ban originates — cite the pair, not §2 alone; the same objection `stories/cli/story.md` raises when refusing to bind its own UAT leg 4 to `cli#gate-1`). Demonstrated on the cross-surface conformance harness — nine files, three story-grain declarations across `cli` / `studio` / `desktop`, one organ: `pnpm --filter @storytree/cli test` runs the judge's rules but NEVER SPAWNS A PROBE, so it cannot go red when the desktop's re-composed route table drifts from the studio's, which is the entire outcome. The only command that can is `pnpm check:mirror-conformance`, and the surface under obligation is the desktop's hand-written copy (all three MIRRORS rows are reference studio, mirror desktop), so the organ was authored as `mirrored-route-conformance` in story `desktop` and all three declarations re-pointed at it. FOUR FENCES. THIS RULE DECIDES WHERE AN INSTRUMENT LIVES AND IS DOWNSTREAM OF RULE (1), NEVER A SUBSTITUTE FOR IT — an instrument whose drift NO suite observes is not thereby homeless; it is a capability that CANNOT STATE ITS PROOF and must not be authored at all. AND A GATE'S GATHERER IS PART OF THE ORGAN ONLY WHEN IT MANUFACTURES OBSERVABILITY THAT DOES NOT OTHERWISE EXIST: the six probes here exist solely because ADR-0176 forbids importing across the wall, so nothing else can see the desktop's payload, and a per-surface split would have produced two units that print JSON and exit with no test file, no assertion and no observable — illegal under the same must-state-its-proof constraint. Contrast `check-boundaries.ts`, which only collects package.json facts anyone can read and is deliberately EXCLUDED from `organism-boundary-tooling` as glue. THIRD, AND ITS OWN DEMONSTRATION FORCES THIS ONE: THE SUITE CRITERION ELIMINATES, IT DOES NOT SELECT — read ‘test surface’ as ANY command that reds on the drift, NEVER as ‘a package suite’. Added 2026-08-07 by the pre-merge librarian pass that reviewed this rule. Applied literally as a SELECTOR the headline does not settle its own case: nothing that reds on a mirrored-payload drift is a story’s suite at all. `pnpm check:mirror-conformance` is a ROOT gate step, deliberately outside the ADR-0195 affected-only narrowing, and belongs to no story’s `--filter … test`. What the criterion actually did here was REFUTE `cli`; what SELECTED `desktop` was the OBLIGATION — all three registry rows are `reference: studio, mirror: desktop`, so the surface under obligation is the desktop’s hand-written copy. The observing command POINTS AWAY from a wrong home; the obligation decides the right one — the same shape as rule (5)’s THE FRACTION POINTS; THE READING DECIDES. This is not a nicety: read ‘suite’ as ‘package suite’ and fence 1 above turns on this rule, because a session would find that NO suite observes this drift and conclude the capability must not have been authored at all — refuting the very unit the rule was written to justify. FOURTH, THIS RULE GOVERNS OVER RULE (5) FOR AN INSTRUMENT, AND THE TWO GENUINELY CONFLICT ON THIS VERY CASE — recorded so the conflict is not rediscovered later as a contradiction. Rule (5) says the CALL SITES decide which story. Enumerated on the bytes 2026-08-07: `mirror-conformance.ts` has exactly THREE call sites and ALL THREE are in `packages/cli/src` (`check-mirror-conformance.ts:65`, `check-verification-decay.ts:88`, `mirror-conformance.test.ts:21`), so rule (5) points 3-of-3 at `cli` while this rule and the obligation point at `desktop`. Rule (5) is not wrong here; it is DEGENERATE. An instrument’s call sites are its own driver and its own test, which sit beside it by construction, so counting them merely re-reports where the file already lives and can never name the surface under obligation. Rule (5) therefore governs a LODGER — code with real consumers spread across stories — and this rule governs an INSTRUMENT; where a subtree is both, this one wins. Read that fence in the other direction too, because it costs this arc a data point: increment 3 did NOT confirm rule (5), it SET IT ASIDE, so nothing here counts as a second instance of the call-site method and the falsifier that would test it (`cli` 29 declarations / `studio` 32) is still unrun. ### FIFTH FENCE ON RULE (5) — THE FALSIFIER RAN IN `studio` AND CAME BACK IDLE: NOT HELD, NOT FAILED, NEVER ENGAGED. Added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 4, which took the `studio` story (31 declarations) expressly to run it. **n stays 1** — increment 2's `open-link-policy.ts` is still the only header-vs-call-sites CONFLICT in existence, and `studio` supplied no second one. THE CASE THAT LOOKED LIKE A CONFLICT IS NOT ONE, and `story-author` refused the increment's framing on the bytes. `apps/studio/src/lib/stressLayout.ts` opens by naming ADR-0171's default-OFF `?layout=stress` map mode — an ORIGIN, which is exactly the bait rule (5) exists to catch — but lines 19-23 of that SAME comment block record that ADR-0283 D2 RETIRED that mode ('nothing on the map reaches this any more') and name the surviving caller, `overviewConstellation.ts`, by file. The header therefore does not conflict with the call sites; it CONTAINS them and agrees, and rule (5)'s aphorism (a header names ORIGIN, the call sites name JOB) presumes a header that is SILENT about the job. RULE (1) HAD ALREADY RESOLVED IT — ON ITS OWN STATED TEST, AND THE PATH MENTION IS NOT THAT TEST. `library-overview`'s OUTCOME has the whole corpus 'laid out ... by a pure, deterministic, cycle-tolerant layout', which plainly covers this module's job; that, and only that, is rule (1)'s ground here. The tempting shortcut is to say the TREE NAMED THE FILE — `stories/library-tech-tree-overlay/library-overview.md:156` does print `apps/studio/src/lib/stressLayout.ts` by path. DO NOT PROMOTE THAT INTO A CRITERION. Verified on the bytes by the pre-merge librarian pass rather than taken from the increment: that path sits inside a clause describing what `constellationLayout` WRAPS, and the very next sentence of the same spec DISCLAIMS the module — 'The layout ENGINE is NOT the red-green surface — dagre is a viable fallback'. A spec naming a module it CONSUMES and calls swappable is documenting a DEPENDENCY EDGE, which is the weakest ownership signal available and, generalised into a rule, is exactly ADR-0317 D2's rejected import-graph derivation wearing prose clothes. A path mention CORROBORATES an outcome that already covers the job; it NEVER substitutes for one, and 'the spec names the file' must not enter this map as a fourth authoring rule by the back door. The enumeration was 1-of-1 — a fraction fence (i) says settles NOTHING by arithmetic — so a session moving on that count alone would have reached the right owner for a reason this rule's own fence disclaims. THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THE RULE, and banking it as a second instance is precisely the corruption increment 3 was corrected for. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, which is the durable part and is the reason to expect SCARCITY — but NOT unfalsifiability: this house writes long headers and MAINTAINS THEM ON A LAG. Both halves re-verified on the bytes by the pre-merge librarian pass, and the evidence is THICKER than increment 4 claimed: ADR-0251's landing commit (3ef84c96) states in its own message that 'Stale prose in overviewConstellation.ts and types.ts corrected in place by the librarian pass', and ADR-0283's retirement was written into EIGHT files' comments in one pass (0cad4b1b), six of them naming ADR-0283 D2 explicitly — not three. THE INFERENCE DRAWN FROM THAT EVIDENCE DOES NOT SURVIVE, AND ITS OWN EXAMPLE IS THE REFUTATION. `stressLayout.ts`'s header DID drift from its call sites: ADR-0283 D2 retired the stress mode in dffabc83 (2026-08-02 21:05) while that header still read, in the present tense, 'buildWorld consumes `stressSeeds` to seed island positions ONLY in stress mode' — and 0cad4b1b corrected it FIFTY-SEVEN MINUTES LATER. The maintenance is therefore a SEPARATE, LATER cleanup pass, never an atomic property of the change itself, so 'a header kept current cannot have drifted from its call sites' is true and VACUOUS — the live question is whether it is current YET. Rule (5)'s conflicts are consequently TRANSIENT RATHER THAN ABSENT, and hunting the falsifier is a SAMPLING problem: you must catch a subtree in the window between a semantic change and its cleanup pass. `studio` was sampled AFTER its cleanup pass had run, which is why it read as barren. `open-link-policy.ts` is not a freak — it is the case whose cleanup never came. That is a class of LAG, not of luck, and it is why the honest verdict on this run is IDLE (the window was closed) and not REFUTED. FOR `guidance-curator`, WHOSE DECISION THIS BLOCKS: treat the lodger call-site rule as UNRECONFIRMED at n=1, and weigh whether a rule stuck at n=1 should graduate into every session's guidance at all — that is now a live question, not a formality awaiting a second data point. Do NOT hunt the falsifier in `studio`: measured across all 31 declarations, none is a conflict case. `cli` is the only untried candidate, and it is entered with NO PREDICTION — deliberately. Rules (5) and (6) EACH shipped a defective first draft by stating more than had been measured, and a forecast written into this map is read by the next session as a finding, which would make that the third instance of the same error. What is KNOWN, and is a reason rather than a forecast: fence 4 makes rule (5) DEGENERATE for the gate instruments that dominate `packages/cli/src`, so those declarations are rule (6)'s work and not rule (5)'s. `cli`'s genuine LODGERS are simply untried, and the sampling caveat above governs them — a lodger whose cleanup pass has already run presents no conflict even where the method would have worked, so a second IDLE result there would still not be evidence against the rule. ### SIXTH FENCE ON RULE (5) — THE MECHANICAL OPENING STEP RETURNS CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWERS TWO WAYS, AND BOTH ARE SILENT. Measured 2026-08-07 in increment 4; recorded here because rule (5) says the check OPENS MECHANICALLY, and this is where that step lies. Neither failure raises an error — each returns a plausible NUMBER, which under this rule reads as a finding. (a) FALSE ZERO, FROM MIXED IMPORT FORMS. `apps/studio` mixes `'../lib/format'` and `'../lib/panelFlyout.js'` inside the same tree, unlike the `.js`-only NodeNext packages the rest of this map covers. Re-measured on the bytes by the pre-merge librarian pass, in a form a later session can RE-DERIVE rather than take on trust: of the 42 non-test modules in `apps/studio/src/lib`, searching ONLY the `.js` form returns ZERO for 26 of them, and searching ONLY the bare form returns zero for 6. And 'no consumers' is not read as a broken query — it is read as a decisive fact about a lodger. AND THE ZERO IS NOT THE WORST CASE. Eleven of those 42 modules have consumers using BOTH forms, so a single-form search there returns a PARTIAL COUNT rather than nothing — which is strictly more dangerous under a rule about FRACTIONS, because it corrupts the numerator and the denominator together and comes back looking exactly like a finding, whereas a zero at least invites disbelief. Match BOTH forms; disbelieve a zero before reporting it, and never report a fraction without confirming the enumeration was total. (b) FALSE HUB, FROM SAME-BASENAME TWINS. `apps/studio/src/lib/sprite-sheet.ts` and `apps/studio/src/lib/trailReveal.ts` are 8- and 9-line re-export shims onto `@storytree/app-surface`, which contains modules of the SAME BASENAME — the very ones they re-export. An unfiltered basename search attributed app-surface's eight internal call sites to the shim, roughly TREBLING the apparent consumer count of a file that contains no logic at all. Re-counted on the bytes by the pre-merge librarian pass: app-surface's internal `sprite-sheet` call sites are exactly EIGHT (a ninth grep hit, `sprite-sizing.ts:13`, is a COMMENT and is correctly not one), against five real studio-side consumers of the shim. The increment's first draft of this fence called the result 'the most-consumed module in the residue'; THAT WAS ITSELF FALSE and is corrected here — measured across the thirteen story-grain modules under this directory, `appData` (24 consumer files) and `poll` (14) both outrank the shim even at its inflated count, which would have placed third. Note WHY that matters more than the arithmetic: an inflated-but-plausible number is not caught by asking whether the count looks about right, and the fence's own first draft proves it by getting the superlative wrong in the same breath as the warning. Filter by PATH, never by basename. THE TWO FAIL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS — one hides real consumers, the other manufactures ones that do not exist — which is exactly why neither is caught by sanity-checking whether the count looks about right. This fence constrains HOW to enumerate and selects nothing; it adds no criterion, and fence (ii) above still governs what the resulting number may be used for. Read the scope twice, because both halves are load-bearing. A CORRECT enumeration is still not a decision — fence (i) is untouched here and is not weakened by implication: getting the count right earns you a number that POINTS, never one that DECIDES, and this fence exists only to stop a wrong number masquerading as a right one. AND THESE TWO TRAPS ARE PROPERTIES OF THE TREE, NOT OF THE LODGER QUESTION — they are recorded under rule (5) because rule (5) is the only rule here that instructs a mechanical enumeration (rule (6) enumerates nothing and explicitly makes rule (5) degenerate for instruments), but any future rule or one-off survey that counts call sites in `apps/studio` inherits them unchanged. ### (7) SEVENTH FENCE — ON RULE (1), NOT ON RULE (5): THE OUTCOME MATCH IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. Added 2026-08-08 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 5, and recorded as a fence on rule (1) rather than as "rule (1) correctly applied", because rule (1) as written does not contain this test — claiming that it does would smuggle a criterion in by the back door, which is the error the FIFTH FENCE corrected when it refused to promote "the spec names the file" into a fourth authoring rule. THE RULE. Before declaring a CAPABILITY the owner of a subtree, name the command that would go red if that file broke, and check it is a command the CAPABILITY ITSELF carries — its own spec-borne `proof.command`, or a reliability gate that `(covers:)` it. If no such command exists, the outcome match is NOMINAL and the declaration is refused. Binding an outcome to a proof that cannot fail on the thing is the rubber stamp ADR-0085 forbids and ADR-0097 §2 re-affirms (cite the pair, as rule (6) already instructs). DEMONSTRATED ON A MATCHED PAIR — record them together, because the pair is the whole teaching. Both are a `packages/cli` file whose job is plainly covered by a capability in ANOTHER story, and they get OPPOSITE answers on this test alone. ACCEPTED: `packages/cli/src/health.ts` -> `library-health-gate` (story `library`). That capability's `proof.command` is `pnpm --filter @storytree/cli test` with `scope.sourceGlobs: ["packages/cli/src/**/*.ts"]`, its contracts already cite this file as `covers:` and `packages/cli/src/health.test.ts` as `proven by:`, and that test imports `./health.js` (`health.test.ts:8-16`) — so a broken re-export fails the suite AT IMPORT TIME, not merely at typecheck. READ THAT CITATION PRECISELY, because part of it is rotten and a reader who checks it must not discard the whole verdict with it: the `covers:` FILE PATH is right and is what this test turns on, but the LINE RANGES on all eight contracts (`health.ts:84-253`) are dead — `packages/cli/src/health.ts` is a 15-line shim, and the ranges do not match the real module at `packages/drive/src/health.ts` either (contract 5 still asserts a count-reconciliation check ADR-0210 REMOVED). That is `stories/library`'s rot to fix, not this map's; it does not touch the verdict here, which rests on the COMMAND and the import edge, never on a line number. Corroborated against an ENFORCED source rather than the spec alone: `packages/orchestrator/src/test-command-registry.ts:55` independently binds `library-health-gate` to `pnpmTest("@storytree/cli")` with `pkgScope("cli")`. REFUSED: `packages/cli/src/worktree-create.ts` -> `noticeboard-cli` (story `notice-board`). That capability's outcome names `worktree create` IN SO MANY WORDS, so rule (1) read literally says yes. But its `proof.command` is `pnpm --filter @storytree/drive test` with drive-only scope and a drive-only `real:` arm, and the file and its tests are in `packages/cli`. The proof cannot see it. IT IS NOT ABOUT WHETHER THE FILE IS TESTED. `worktree-create.ts` carries 935 lines of tests across three suites (`worktree-create.test.ts` 139, `worktree-create-command.test.ts` 512, `worktree-create-io-default.test.ts` 284 — counted on the bytes by the pre-merge librarian pass), which is exactly what makes the declaration tempting. That coverage belongs to `cli`'s suite, not to `noticeboard-cli`'s proof. The question is whether the CAPABILITY'S OWN NAMED PROOF sees the file. (The increment's first draft added "and is among the best-covered files in the residue"; CUT as an unmeasured comparative — the same class of defect as the false superlative the SIXTH FENCE corrects, and the argument never needed it.) FENCE (a): IT ELIMINATES A CANDIDATE; IT NEVER SELECTS A HOME AND NEVER FORCES AUTHORING. The same shape as rule (6) fence 3. A STORY-grain declaration carries no proof claim and is therefore never eliminated by this test — by rule (1) a story-grain declaration exists precisely where no capability covers the subtree at all, so applying a capability-proof test to it would make the map unfillable. FENCE (b): "BINDS NO VERDICT" IS NOT A LICENCE. The block `$comment` says this map binds no verdict, and that clause is real — it is why GLOBS are legal here and refused in `proof.real.sourceFile`. It governs what the map may CONTAIN, never whether the map may assert something untrue. A report-only artifact that reports a falsehood is worse than one that says nothing. The precedent is this arc's own: increment 4 refused `sprite-sheet.ts` / `trailReveal.ts` -> `studio-app-surface-adapter` on exactly this ground — "that capability's suite cannot go red when a re-export breaks" — and those were OWNERSHIP declarations, not proof bindings. WHERE IT ALSO BIT, so the cost is visible: `packages/cli/src/adopt-plan.ts` -> `adoption-pocket-classifier` was refused for a stronger version of the same reason — that capability has NO `proof:` block at all, and its only instrument is `drive-machinery#gate-1`, whose command is `pnpm --filter @storytree/orchestrator test`. Named, not fixed: `drive-machinery#gate-2` runs `pnpm --filter @storytree/cli test`, so adding the capability to that gate's `(covers:)` would bring it within an observing command. That is an edit to `stories/drive-machinery`'s authored gate list — `story-author`'s to make on that story's spec, and it changes what an already-signed observe gate claims. It is not this map's to make, and this arc never hand-writes a node file. (The increment's first draft called it "the owner's call"; CUT — nothing establishes owner authority here, and that story's own text calls the gates "the author's expandable floor".) ### EIGHTH FENCE ON RULE (5) — THE FALSIFIER IN `cli` CAME BACK DEGENERATE, WHICH IS NOT `studio`'s IDLE. Added 2026-08-08 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 5, which took `cli` — the candidate fence 5 named as the only untried one — expressly to run it. n STAYS 1: increment 2's `open-link-policy.ts` is still the only header-vs-call-sites CONFLICT ON RECORD. (Fence 5 wrote "in existence"; CORRECTED here by the pre-merge librarian pass — 21 stories of the residue are unmeasured, and fence 5 says so itself three sentences later, so "in existence" contradicted its own paragraph. Read both as "on record".) MEASURED, on all 18 non-instrument story-grain subtrees declared to `cli`: ZERO have a consumer outside `packages/cli`, and no sibling call site inside it can name a different story either. Both halves are established STRUCTURALLY rather than by enumeration, which matters because enumeration is exactly what the SIXTH FENCE showed is easy to get confidently wrong. OUTSIDE the package: no workspace `package.json` declares `@storytree/cli` as a dependency, so under pnpm workspaces an import of it from another package would not RESOLVE — enforced by the package manager, not observed by a grep. Two live tests enforce it besides: `apps/studio/src/modelPathBoundary.test.ts:21` walks every file under `apps/studio/src` and fails on a static or dynamic import of `@storytree/cli`, and `apps/studio/src/components/ChatPanel.spawn.test.tsx:174-176` asserts the same of `ChatPanel.tsx`. INSIDE the package: `packageOwnership` classifies `@storytree/cli` as ONE organism owned by story `cli`, held to the disk by `check:boundaries` at 24/24, so a sibling importer is in the same story by construction and can never name a candidate story either. WHAT THE ENUMERATION MAY NOT BE READ AS. The increment's first draft reported the call sites as a three-way split — "the DISPATCHER (10 subtrees), a SIBLING (9), or NOTHING AT ALL (5: db-cli, build-agents, build-claude-md, build-unit-status, worktree-prune-entry)". CUT, because it reads as a partition of the 18 and is not one: 10+9+5 = 24, the first count is in SUBTREES while the last is in MODULES (three of its five sit under the single subtree `packages/cli/src/build-*.ts` and a fourth under `worktree*.ts`), and the buckets are not disjoint at subtree grain — `worktree*.ts` alone holds a dispatcher-reached module, a sibling-reached one and an unimported one. A number that looks like a finding and does not add up is precisely what the SIXTH FENCE was written about. The ZERO is the finding; the split was decoration and is not restated. Likewise the draft's "one cross-subtree edge exists (`worktree-create.ts:34` imports `./arc.js`)" was UNDERCOUNTED — the very next line, `:35`, imports `./envelope.js`, a subtree owned by `unified-command-dispatch`. Both edges stay inside the package and inside story `cli`, which is the only property the argument needs. THE VERDICT IS DEGENERATE, AND THE DISTINCTION FROM `studio` IS THE POINT. Rule (5) defines a LODGER as code sitting in a package it reaches MANY CONSUMERS from, and identifies its owner by seeing which story's code consumes it. `packages/cli` has no such code, and the reason is DECLARED in the work graph as well as verified above: `stories/cli/story.md:24` carries `consumed_by: []` and `:125` states "the CLI is a pure source — nothing imports it" (ADR-0112 decision 3, "`apps/studio` drops its `cli` dependency", removed the last inbound edge). A package nothing imports cannot host a lodger, so rule (5)'s enumeration here can only ever return "100% inside `packages/cli`", which re-reports where the file already sits and names no candidate story. That is the SAME degeneracy fence 4 recorded for instruments, reached by a second and independent route: an instrument's call sites are its own driver and test, beside it by construction; a CLI VERB SURFACE's call sites are the dispatcher and its siblings, beside it by construction. Fence 4 made rule (5) degenerate for the instruments that dominate this story's declarations; this measurement extends it to the verb surfaces, which is the rest of the STORY-GRAIN RESIDUE here — not the rest of the package, most of which is already capability-grain. IDLE AND DEGENERATE ARE DIFFERENT VERDICTS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ACTIONABLE. `studio` came back IDLE because the method could have worked and the sampling window was closed (fence 5: the conflicts are transient, the cleanup passes run late). `cli` comes back DEGENERATE because the method cannot produce a candidate story here AT ALL, at any sampling time — the reason is structural, not contingent. IDLE means try again later; DEGENERATE means do not try here. Neither is a refutation. WHAT THIS CORRECTS IN FENCE 5. Fence 5 named `cli` the only untried candidate on the stated expectation that "`cli`'s genuine LODGERS are simply untried". Measured, `cli` has no genuine lodgers among these declarations at all. The expectation was wrong about the SHAPE of the block, and that correction — not a data point — is this increment's contribution to the rule's file. WHAT MUST NOT BE INFERRED. Not that rule (5) is unfalsifiable: increment 4's pass already refuted that on `stressLayout.ts`'s own 57-minute header drift, and it must not return by a side door. Not that rule (5) should be retired — `guidance-curator`'s decision, not this arc's. And NO PREDICTION about the long tail: 21 stories hold the remaining story-grain declarations at one to ten each (`drive-machinery` 10, `app-surface` 7, then three and below), none of them measured here, and increment 4's first draft carried exactly such a forecast about `cli` and had it cut on the ground that a forecast written into this map is read by the next session as a finding.

baseline.$comment: The measurement `storytree ownership` prints its trend against — the evidence base a future blocking rung would have to argue from. Re-record it deliberately, not on every edit: a moved baseline erases the trend it exists to show. RE-RECORDED 2026-08-18 (`ownership-walk-extension-aperture`): the prior baseline (521 files / 483 unowned, 2026-08-06) predates the walk's extension-aperture widening from `.ts`/`.tsx`-only to also cover `.mts`/`.cts`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` (test variants excluded, `.d.*` included). The aperture genuinely enlarged the measured population — 22 previously-invisible files entered the walk, all 22 now declared — so an upward re-baseline is the sanctioned move (ADR-0269: 'a drain ceiling rises only when the measured population enlarges, never to absorb growth'). This is not the normal day-to-day drift the trend line already absorbs: files also grew from the widening itself (622 -> 643 is the aperture; the remaining movement since 2026-08-06 is ordinary landings, already reflected in the 45 unowned this baseline records against the WIDENED walk).

subtrees.$section_cli: packages/cli — the verb surface. Most modules here FRONT another organism's competence, so the honest owner is that organism's capability, not the `cli` story: `drift.ts` is binding-staleness's, `tree.ts` is notice-board's, `deploy-health.ts` is studio-cloud's. What is left over is the `$section_cli_residual` block below — gate rungs, drains, projections, doctors and still-unhomed verb organs, a MIXED grain as `capability-layer-coverage-arc` resolves entries in place; read the live split from `storytree ownership`, never from a marker.
subtrees.$section_cli_residual: The `packages/cli/src` residual working area — gate rungs, drains, generated-view builders, doctors, and CLI-resident verb surfaces (retire) whose organism was, or still is, unsettled. NOT a grain claim: entries move from story grain to capability grain IN PLACE as `capability-layer-coverage-arc` resolves them, and stay in this alphabetical section rather than migrating out. The one exception to `in place` is a file that physically LEAVES the package: `arc.ts`, `question.ts` and `increment.ts` were listed here until 2026-08-14, when ADR-0369 extracted them into packages/arc, so their entries moved to $section_arc with the code — the map is held to the disk, and a declaration matching no file is reported STALE by `storytree ownership`, not silently tolerated. Read the live split from that command, never from this marker; see the block $comment.
subtrees.$section_arc: packages/arc — the arc organism (ADR-0369, `arc-tier-extraction-arc`). The arc domain was a TENANT of two buildings until 2026-08-14: the three write verbs in packages/cli, the derived join in packages/drive for reach. It now owns one, and every file here is capability grain except the barrel. This section is the reason the `stories/arc` story could exist at all — ADR-0192 D2 (packages-forward) refuses a new story whose code sits in another story's package, so the package had to be built first.
subtrees.$section_drive: packages/drive — the shared build/orchestrate drivers (ADR-0112). Nearly every module is a named drive-machinery capability or the driver half of another story's capability; the residue is composition glue.
subtrees.$section_orchestrator: packages/orchestrator — the deterministic spine and the proof ruler. The best-mapped package in the repo: drive-machinery decomposed the spine capability-by-capability, so almost every file has a real owner one grain below the story.
subtrees.$section_agent: packages/agent — the leaf executors behind the PhaseAuthor seam.
subtrees.$section_library: packages/library — the knowledge tier. `src/store` is the seam (seed entry); the root barrel splits by competence between the library story's own capabilities and the UAT/proof-binding stories that host their pure computes here.
subtrees.$section_ports_and_boards: The two root ports and the two small board/member organisms. Each is one competence end to end, so a directory-grain entry IS the honest grain here rather than a shortcut.
subtrees.$section_studio_server: apps/studio/server — the shared API route table. Owned largely by studio-cloud, library-review and studio-members capabilities rather than by the `studio` surface story.
subtrees.$section_studio_components: apps/studio/src/components — the renderer. The Library lens components map one-to-one onto library-tech-tree-overlay capabilities; the forest map does not. TreeView.tsx is declared at STORY grain deliberately: SEVEN units name it, so no single capability is responsible for it, and that is the ADR-0317 non-injectivity finding standing in one file.
subtrees.$section_studio_shell: apps/studio — the SPA shell, the Playwright/Vitest configs and the story-UAT spec.
subtrees.$section_desktop: apps/desktop — the thick client. The backend routes are desktop capabilities one-to-one; the Electron shell, keychain and credential ports are the two credential/shell capabilities; `src/apply` (the ADR-0117 brokered rebuild loop) has no capability yet.
subtrees.$section_world_and_art: The render core, the shared app surface, the R3F website engine and the art factory.
subtrees.$section_uat_organisms: The UAT-witness organisms — the best-decomposed corner of the tree, where nearly every file is its own capability.
subtrees.$section_traversal: The four context-traversal organisms — every non-barrel file is a named capability.
subtrees.$comment_decision_reads: STORY GRAIN, KNOWINGLY, and it is residue rather than a preference (`adrs-into-the-dag-arc-inc-07`). The decision-record read extractor and its batch ingest want two capabilities of their own — `transcript-decision-read-extraction` and `transcript-decision-read-ingest` — on the same rule the section header states. Minting them is a WORK-HIERARCHY edit under `stories/**`, which is `story-author`'s remit (`route-structural-forks-to-story-author`) and drags a proof binding behind it; the increment that built these files was fenced to ingest-and-report. So they take the story id the barrel already takes, and this comment is the standing note that the finer owner is owed. Read the consequence precisely: ADR-0346 D2 retired story-grain WORK claims, so nobody can claim these two subtrees at the grain declared here until the capabilities exist.
subtrees.$comment_aperture: NINTH BLOCK — the extension-aperture widening (`ownership-walk-extension-aperture`, 2026-08-18). `gatherSourceFiles` (packages/cli/src/ownership.ts) widened from `.ts`/`.tsx`-only to also walk `.mts`/`.cts`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` (test variants excluded, `.d.*` included, matching the pre-existing `.d.ts` treatment). The entries below are the newly-visible files this widening exposed, each declared per rule (1)/(7): capability grain ONLY where an existing capability's OWN scope.sourceGlobs already names the file (`camera-rasterisation-probe` for measure-camera-rasterisation.mjs), story grain everywhere else because no capability's stated proof reaches these author-time/harness/e2e scripts. This is a SEPARATE authoring pass from the eight numbered blocks above (those predate the aperture and cover only `.ts`/`.tsx`); it is deliberately not folded into the numbered rules, which is why it is its own top-level comment rather than a ninth numbered rule there.

hostedStories.$comment: ADR-0192 decision 2 — the packages-forward GRANDFATHER register: the FROZEN list of stories whose unit proof-bound sources (proof.real.sourceFile + literal sourceGlobs) already lived inside ANOTHER story's building (a foreign packages/<x> or apps/<x> dir) at adoption (2026-07-13), derived mechanically via the landlord rule's evidence (rule 5, PR #720). check-boundaries.ts passes this register's keys to the pure judge (packages/cli/src/boundaries.ts): a hosted story ABSENT from the register is REFUSED regardless of declared edges (a NEW story's code lives in its OWN workspace package — packages-forward), and a register entry with NO hosting evidence is a STALE violation (remove it) — so the register is the self-pruning migration worklist (ADR-0192 decision 3: migrate one story at a time, whole footprint at once). Entries only ever LEAVE as stories migrate; ADDING one is a loud, owner-reviewed diff. Every entry below already carries a declared host edge (the increment-1 remediation), so the landlord rule is green over them.

register.wisp-as-story-claim: hosted in agent (packages/agent) + drive-machinery (packages/drive) + notice-board (packages/notice-board) + studio (apps/studio)
